value: hard close feathers held close to body
yellow beak and legs, sometimes with black markings
made a Natural Monument of Japan in 1950
bred as a sparring partner for larger fighting cocks
used to create the Kumano Jidori meat hybrid

history_summary.value: The Yakido descends from the Shamo group of Japanese fighting fowl, themselves derived from Malay-type birds brought from Thailand in the 1600s, and was bred in Mie Prefecture in the mid-1800s as a smaller sparring partner for bigger gamecocks. Japan declared it a Natural Monument in 1950.
